title: First trip to Europe as first recalled, with Norman Granz
summary: Stewart first places his European debut in the mid-'50s on a Granz package with Erroll Garner, and says he was treated royally.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Now, when did you first go to Europe?
Let's see now. I think this goes back to the year in the mid-'50s.
Oh, you didn't go until the mid-'50s?

If I'm not mistaken, I think it was around the mid-'50s, yes, and I think it was a Norman Granz thing. And it so happened that Erroll Garner was on the package. He wasn't playing with me, but he was along with the group when -- that was my first time to go to Europe.
How many countries did you tour, do you remember?
Oh, I think we just played -- well, possibly England -- I think it was around England mostly.
Oh, you played -- oh, mostly Britain.
Yeah, yeah. It was about a three or four-day affair, you know.
Uh-huh. And did you -- how did you -- were you excited about going to Europe?
I was, yes.
Did it live up to your expectations? Did you find it unusual?

Well, I found it -- I enjoyed that and especially the people whom I came in contact with. Most of the people knew us very well, especially by our recordings and what have you and we -- I'm sure I'm speaking for all of us -- we were really treated royally.
Oh, yeah, well, everybody who goes -- works for Norman Granz, Granz always makes sure that you get
first-class accommodations.
That's right.
Working in that kind of a situation.
Yeah.
But now how did you feel about working for Norman Gram ? How did Norman, or Mr. Gram , that is, come off to you?
Well, there wasn't -- as far as I was concerned, there wasn't any problems personally or what have you. Just another fella, as far as I'm concerned. I only worked with him that once, anyway.
Well, you know, he has a reputation for paying very well.
Oh, yes. Right.
Who were you playing with? Was this the Jazz at the Philharmonic?

I think that was probably what it was. Well, Erroll Garner on piano and I can't quite remember the other musicians. But I'd say there were about eight or nine of us on this gig. That's about as far as I can recall.
